architectReview.evidence: Delegated architect review (agent 5-ReviewCoverage, opus) confirmed the two hard requirements: rust_llvm_cov is exhaustively best-effort (every failure path -> Ok(None); no ?/unwrap/panic; live Ok(None) proven under the sandbox peony linker) and both blocking ops (tree-sitter walk + cargo subprocess) run off the tokio runtime via spawn_blocking. Panic-safety solid (non-UTF8 skipped, malformed tolerated, follow_links=false). It returned REQUEST CHANGES for ONE MEDIUM: nested-function branch double-attribution (count both enclosing + nested). FIXED this pass: replaced the inner full-subtree walk with a pruning `count_branches` that stops descending at nested-function boundaries. Verified live: a Python `outer` with a nested `inner` now reports outer=1/inner=1 (was outer=2). Also fixed 2 LOW hardening items the review raised: units_in_file now skips a file on set_language error instead of aborting the whole walk, and filter_entry never filters the depth-0 root. The 2 remaining LOW P3 items (unbounded AST recursion depth; uncovered_names omitting Rust fns when the llvm-cov aggregate succeeds) are the ones the architect explicitly called optional hardening/advisory and are accepted. Reverified: build clean, clippy 0, cargo test 13/13.
